title: Source tax: residence abroad and cross-border questions
purpose: Group the country of residence as the calculator does. Ask Liechtenstein and Germany residents the cross-border questions (daily return, non-return days, certificate of residence) and derive whether the employee is in principle not liable to source tax (Liechtenstein) or the cross-border tariff applies (Germany).

stories.title: Derive the calculator's residence answers from the home address and ask cross-border questions only of Germany and Liechtenstein residents
stories.i_want: Lonio to group the employee's country of residence the way the Zurich calculator does (Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein or other country), without asking it again, and to ask the cross-border commuting questions only of employees living in Germany or Liechtenstein
stories.so_that: the tariff code can be computed by following the calculator's logic from the home address the employee already gave, and no employee is asked cross-border questions that no party needs for them
stories.priority_reason: Lonio computes the full tariff code instead of HR using the calculator (D-001); without the residence grouping no tariff code can be computed for any employee subject to source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: Residence is grouped as in the calculator from the country of the home address
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address in step 2 'Home address', as it applies on their first working day (assumption D-041, to be verified by a domain expert)
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the residence for source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: the residence is 'Switzerland' when the country is Switzerland, 'Germany' when it is Germany, 'Liechtenstein' when it is Liechtenstein, and 'Other country' for any other country; the employee is not asked a separate question about their main residence or country of residence for source tax

acceptance_criteria.title: Switzerland and other countries get no cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland or in a country other than Germany and Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: step 5 'Cross-border commuting' is not shown and no question on daily return, non-return days, reasonableness of daily return or certificate of residence is asked; for source tax the base tariff applies without further residence questions, as in the calculator

examples.name: Calculator: 'Anderes Land' gives the base tariff (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-f86c6b)

acceptance_criteria.title: Germany and Liechtenstein residents get step 5 'Cross-border commuting'
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany or Liechtenstein (and is therefore subject to source tax, as every employee living abroad is)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee has completed step 4 'Civil status and spouse'
acceptance_criteria.then: step 5 'Cross-border commuting' is shown before step 6 'Source tax details'; a Germany resident is asked the Germany questions starting with daily return to Germany, a Liechtenstein resident the Liechtenstein questions starting with daily return to Liechtenstein, and never the questions of the other country (step order is assumption D-047, to be verified by a domain expert)

examples.name: Calculator: Germany shows the daily return question (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-31d762)
Calculator: Liechtenstein shows the daily return question (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-e22d17)

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border answers that no longer apply are not kept
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee answered cross-border questions and then changes their home address country so that those questions no longer apply (for example from Germany to Switzerland)
acceptance_criteria.then: the cross-border answers that no longer apply are discarded and not recorded; before submission they are kept, so changing the country back restores them; after submission any change of the country is made by HR, and the residence grouping and every result of this section are derived again from the latest answers (D-036, D-037); if an HR change makes cross-border questions apply that were never asked, the tariff code shows 'incomplete - HR must complete' until HR enters the missing answers (assumption D-048, to be verified by a domain expert)

stories.title: Germany: daily return and certificate of residence
stories.i_want: an employee living in Germany to be asked whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Germany and, if so, whether they have a certificate of residence for HR
stories.so_that: Lonio can decide, as the calculator does, whether the cross-border tariff applies and HR knows when a certificate is still expected
stories.priority_reason: The answer changes the tariff letter (e.g. C1Y becomes N1Y in the calculator); without it Lonio cannot compute the tariff code it now owns (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Daily return to Germany is asked of every Germany resident
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's home address is in Germany
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Germany, answering 'yes' or 'no'; the answer is required and is recorded for source tax; it is a statement of what the employee expects, no document is asked; employees living in any other country are not asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Certificate of residence is asked only with daily return
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers that they return daily
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they have a certificate of residence for HR, answering 'yes', 'no' or 'not yet'; the answer is required and is recorded for source tax and for HR, so HR knows a certificate is still expected; the certificate itself goes to HR outside Lonio and is not uploaded; when the employee does not return daily the question is not asked

examples.name: Calculator: certificate question after daily return 'Ja' (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-5f6820)
No daily return - no certificate question

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border tariff with daily return depends on the certificate
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany and returns daily
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether the cross-border tariff applies
acceptance_criteria.then: with a certificate of residence the cross-border tariff applies; with 'no' or 'not yet' the normal tariff applies ('not yet' counts as 'no', D-035); the cross-border letters follow the calculator in full (A to L, B to M, C to N, H to P, G to Q; assumption D-051, to be verified by a domain expert); if the certificate is handed in later, HR changes the answer after submission and the tariff code is derived again (D-037)

examples.name: Calculator: daily return and certificate gives N1Y (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-993db3)
Calculator: daily return without certificate gives C1Y (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-993db3)

acceptance_criteria.title: Only Germany residents can get the cross-border tariff
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee does not live in Germany
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether the cross-border tariff applies
acceptance_criteria.then: the cross-border tariff never applies; the normal tariff applies (for Liechtenstein residents subject to the double taxation agreement rule)

examples.name: Calculator: 'Anderes Land' gives the base tariff (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-f86c6b)
Calculator: Liechtenstein over 45 days gives the normal tariff (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-cc19c7)

stories.title: Germany: no daily return - reasonableness and more than 60 non-return days
stories.i_want: an employee living in Germany who does not return daily to be asked whether a daily return would basically be reasonable (less than 100 km driving distance) and, if so, whether they expect more than 60 work-related non-return days in the calendar year
stories.so_that: Lonio can decide, as the calculator does, whether the cross-border tariff or the normal tariff applies
stories.priority_reason: The answers decide between the cross-border and the normal tariff letter (calculator: N1Y vs C1Y); Lonio cannot compute the tariff code without them (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Reasonableness of daily return is asked only without daily return
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers that they do not return daily to their main residence in Germany
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether a daily return would basically be reasonable (less than 100 km driving distance), answering 'yes' or 'no'; the answer is required and recorded for source tax; it is not asked when the employee returns daily or lives in another country

acceptance_criteria.title: More than 60 non-return days is asked only when daily return is reasonable
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany and does not return daily
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers that a daily return would be reasonable
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they expect more than 60 work-related non-return days in the calendar year, answering 'yes' or 'no'; the answer is a statement of what the employee expects, not proof, and no document is asked or uploaded (D-035); it is required and recorded for source tax; it is not asked when a daily return is not reasonable

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border tariff without daily return
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany and does not return daily
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether the cross-border tariff applies
acceptance_criteria.then: if a daily return is not reasonable, the normal tariff applies; if it is reasonable and the employee expects more than 60 non-return days, the normal tariff applies; if it is reasonable and the employee does not expect more than 60 non-return days, the cross-border tariff applies, with the letters as in the calculator (assumption D-051, to be verified by a domain expert)

examples.name: Calculator: reasonable and more than 60 days gives C1Y (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-c8aa5e)
Calculator: reasonable and not more than 60 days gives N1Y (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-c8aa5e)

stories.title: Liechtenstein: daily return and more than 45 non-return days
stories.i_want: an employee living in Liechtenstein to be asked, before denomination, spouse and children, whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Liechtenstein and, if not, whether they expect more than 45 work-related non-return days in the calendar year
stories.so_that: Lonio can record, as the calculator does, either 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' or the normal tariff code subject to the double taxation agreement, flagged for HR, without asking tariff questions that are not needed
stories.priority_reason: HR's rule makes every Liechtenstein resident subject to source tax while the calculator says in principle not; this conflict must be handled for each Liechtenstein resident (D-007) and the result decides whether a tariff code exists at all.

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein residents are asked the daily return question first
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's home address is in Liechtenstein (so HR's rule makes them subject to source tax and they get the source tax questions, D-007)
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Liechtenstein, answering 'yes' or 'no'; the answer is required and recorded for source tax; this comes before the questions on denomination, spouse gainful employment and children (assumption D-040, to be verified by a domain expert); employees living elsewhere are not asked

examples.name: Calculator: Liechtenstein shows the daily return question (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-e22d17)

acceptance_criteria.title: More than 45 non-return days is asked only without daily return
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers that they do not return daily
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they expect more than 45 work-related non-return days in the calendar year, answering 'yes' or 'no'; the answer is a statement of what the employee expects and no document is asked (D-035); it is required and recorded for source tax; with daily return it is not asked

acceptance_criteria.title: In principle no source tax liability: tariff questions are skipped
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee returns daily, or does not return daily and does not expect more than 45 non-return days
acceptance_criteria.then: instead of a tariff code Lonio records 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR; the source tax details (denomination, spouse gainfully employed, children) are not asked (assumption D-040, to be verified by a domain expert); how HR handles the flag belongs to the later HR-side spec (D-034)

acceptance_criteria.title: More than 45 non-return days: normal tariff subject to the double taxation agreement
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Liechtenstein and does not return daily
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee expects more than 45 non-return days
acceptance_criteria.then: the source tax details are asked as for any employee subject to source tax and the normal tariff code is recorded with the note 'subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR (assumption D-040, to be verified by a domain expert)

examples.name: Calculator: more than 45 days gives C1Y with DTA note (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-cc19c7)
Living in Germany - Liechtenstein rule does not apply
